# Accounts & cost

Several AI accounts with failover, secret aliases, usage and quota, context compaction, and deferred tools to keep prompts small.

Pack id `accounts`. Back to [all packs](README.md).

## Plugins

1. [`@dshfiles/ai-accounts`](../../plugins/@dshfiles/ai-accounts/README.md) — Per-account Codex, Claude, Antigravity, Mistral Vibe CLI, OpenCode Go and Command Code provider instances, plus Cursor quota, for DeepSeek Harness, in the spirit of T3 Code.
2. [`@dshfiles/secret-catalog`](../../plugins/@dshfiles/secret-catalog/README.md) — Browse and manage secret CLI aliases for the selected project, without values crossing to the Client.
3. [`@dshfiles/usage`](../../plugins/@dshfiles/usage/README.md) — Request log and cost, token, cache and latency charts built from DSH session logs, indexed incrementally into SQLite.
4. [`@dshfiles/context-compaction`](../../plugins/@dshfiles/context-compaction/README.md) — Chunked compaction backend that keeps summary requests within the model context window.
5. [`@dshfiles/tool-search`](../../plugins/@dshfiles/tool-search/README.md) — Opt-in per-agent progressive discovery of native tools

## Prerequisites

1. An AI account is configured.

## Key settings

1. **Fail over to the next account when one runs out**: Settings entry `ai-accounts`, field `failover`.

## Features

From the onboarding feature catalog: 49 features, the 35 curated ones first.

### Curated

1. **Use another account for this thread** (`ai-accounts`, composer) — Right-click an account in the sidebar to use it for this thread only, keeping the model when it can.
2. **Connect an account without leaving the chat** (`ai-accounts`, settings) — Sign in to a provider from a short dialog without leaving the thread.
3. **Edit and remove accounts** (`ai-accounts`, settings) — Edit an account's settings or remove it, and a new account is saved only once it signs in.
4. **Manage account Models, Settings and Usage** (`ai-accounts`, settings) — Each account has Models, Settings and Usage tabs, with rename and sign-out.
5. **Use a Google AI plan through the Antigravity CLI** (`ai-accounts`, settings) — Use Gemini and the other models of a Google AI plan through the official Antigravity CLI.
6. **Spend the Vibe & Studio allowance through the Vibe CLI** (`ai-accounts`, settings) — Use the Vibe and Studio allowance of a signed-in Mistral Vibe login by running the official Vibe CLI for a thread.
7. **Run Vibe with DSH's tools through its ACP server** (`ai-accounts`, settings) — Let a Vibe thread call DSH tools, so its edits and commands go through DSH approvals, diffs and undo.
8. **Curate models and choose account routes** (`ai-accounts`, settings) — Choose the models each provider offers, their context windows, and how requests spread across accounts with the same model.
9. **Read provider quota and usage status** (`ai-accounts`, observe) — See each account's quota, when it resets and when it was last read, with Refresh and Retry.
10. **Short names in the sidebar usage strip** (`ai-accounts`, settings) — Show or hide the short name beside each meter in the usage strip, and set each account's short name.
11. **Review usage history and cost forecasts** (`ai-accounts`, observe) — Chart past usage and cost, set your own prices, and see what a draft or a turn costs.
12. **Forecast when each account runs out** (`ai-accounts`, observe) — See when each account will run out at the current pace and which account to use next.
13. **Route exhausted Luna accounts through Reserve** (`ai-accounts`, settings) — Once the weekly Luna limit is spent, requests move to the separate Reserve model and its own limit.
14. **Recover failed account requests per failure kind** (`ai-accounts`, settings) — Choose what happens when a request fails: retry, switch account, wait, or stop.
15. **Retry exhausted quota when its reset arrives** (`ai-accounts`, inbox) — A thread stopped by a usage limit resumes on its own when the limit resets, or now on another account.
16. **Open credential setup from failed turns** (`ai-accounts`, transcript) — A turn that failed on missing or rejected credentials links straight to AI Accounts.
17. **Explain turns stopped by a stalled model stream** (`ai-accounts`, transcript) — A turn whose model went silent says for how long and offers Resume or another model.
18. **Turn on the fallback chain for stalled streams** (`ai-accounts`, settings) — Let a stalled model fall back to the thread's next model.
19. **Quota-blocked threads in the Inbox, resumable in place** (`ai-accounts`, inbox) — A thread stopped by a usage limit shows in the Inbox with when it resets and a Resume button.
20. **Warn before re-sending an idle thread past its prompt-cache lifetime** (`ai-accounts`, composer) — After a long pause, a chip warns that the next message costs more because the prompt cache expired.
21. **Browse secrets by scope and environment** (`secret-catalog`, settings) — Search your secrets across project, global and local scopes, without seeing their values.
22. **Reveal on click and copy without revealing** (`secret-catalog`, settings) — Click a masked secret to reveal it for a short time, or copy it without revealing it.
23. **Add a secret inline under the list** (`secret-catalog`, settings) — Add a secret in a new row under the list with a name and a value, or generate one.
24. **Create, edit, rename and remove secrets** (`secret-catalog`, settings) — Add, edit, rename or remove a secret, and delete its stored value only when you ask.
25. **Create and bind from a secret-reference field** (`secret-catalog`, settings) — A secret field can create a new secret in place and keep only a reference to it.
26. **Repair a secret reference that does not resolve** (`secret-catalog`, settings) — A secret reference that does not work says why and offers the fix, such as setting its value.
27. **Let an agent ask the user to store a secret** (`secret-catalog`, transcript) — The agent can ask you to store a secret, and only gets a reference to it back.
28. **Add a Jev key from the Backlog setting** (`secret-catalog`, settings) — Add a Jev key from the Backlog setting, stored as a secret.
29. **Set up a Jev key from chat** (`secret-catalog`, transcript) — When Jev has no key, the latest turn offers a short form to add one.
30. **Request log** (`usage`, observe) — The Requests tab lists every model request with its tokens, cost, time and status.
31. **Usage charts** (`usage`, observe) — The Overview tab charts cost, tokens and requests over time, against the previous period.
32. **Jev API usage card** (`usage`, observe) — See how many Jev calls Backlog and Memory made and what they cost this month.
33. **Tool and skill analytics** (`usage`, observe) — The Tools tab charts how often each tool and skill runs and how long it takes.
34. **Quota in the Usage page** (`usage`, observe) — The Quota tab of Usage shows each account's limits, their history and a forecast.
35. **Cost tab in the thread panel** (`usage`, thread-panel) — The thread panel's Cost tab shows what each turn of this thread cost.

### More

1. **Turn an account on or off from the usage popover** (`ai-accounts`) — Turned-off accounts stay visible in the usage strip, and the usage popover turns each one back on.
2. **See which account serves this thread** (`ai-accounts`) — The usage strip highlights the account the open thread is using right now.
3. **Stop at the plan limits instead of drawing paid extra usage** (`ai-accounts`) — Off by default: an account stops at its plan limit instead of paying for extra usage.
4. **Expose safe secret catalog tools to agents** (`secret-catalog`) — Agents list your secrets without their values, run commands with them injected, and read one value only when asked by name.
5. **Usage index from thread logs** (`usage`) — Every model request and tool call in your threads is counted for the Usage page.
6. **Export usage as metrics** (`usage`) — The agent can export your usage as OpenTelemetry metrics.
7. **Bounded compaction summaries** (`context-compaction`) — Long histories are summarized in pieces small enough for the model to accept.
8. **Background compaction summaries** (`context-compaction`) — Off by default: a thread near its limit prepares its summary in the background so compaction is instant.
9. **Loaded skills kept in compaction checkpoints** (`context-compaction`) — Off by default: compaction keeps the skills a thread loaded, so it does not load them again.
10. **Provider context-overflow recognition** (`context-compaction`) — A context overflow from any provider triggers one compaction and a retry.
11. **Idle compaction before cache expiry** (`context-compaction`) — Off by default: a large idle thread compacts before its prompt cache expires.
12. **Next automatic compaction for a thread** (`context-compaction`) — The agent can ask how many tokens remain before a thread compacts.
13. **Search and disclose tools per agent** (`tool-search`) — The agent starts with a small set of tools and finds others by searching for them.
14. **Tools per agent: enabled and pinned** (`tool-search`) — Tools an agent turns off never reach its threads, and the tools it pins are there from the first request.

## Enable it

1. In the app: **Knowledge › Getting started**, then **Enable pack** on Accounts & cost under Packs. It previews exactly what changes; **Disable pack** reverses it.
2. From an Agent: the `onboarding_pack_apply` tool with pack `accounts`. It runs only when you ask, after showing the preview.
3. From a shell: `dshx init --profile <name> --packs accounts` (Core is added; `--dry-run` previews). See [`dshx init`](../../tooling/dshx/docs/cli-reference.md#dshx-init-compose-a-profile-from-packs).

## Restart

Installing a plugin the profile does not have yet needs a DSH Host restart: DSH reads the profile once at boot. Plugins already installed are switched on in the running DSH. Nothing restarts on its own: use **Restart when idle** in the sidebar when DSH runs under the managed launcher, otherwise your own launcher.
